topic: Kerala HC: women cannot be barred from working in toddy shops - Rule 7(37), Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules, 2002 struck down as violating Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21; State must make workplaces safe, not exclude women (Sophy v. State of Kerala, WP(C) No. 27762 of 2024, 2026 LiveLaw (Ker) 606)

slides.kicker: High Court · Women's right to work
slides.title: Ban on women workers **struck down**
slides.subtitle: Kerala High Court strikes down the rule that kept women out of **toddy shops**. Safety means a safe workplace, **not a ban**.

slides.label: The case
slides.title: A widow was **refused** her husband's job
bullets: Her husband worked at a toddy shop in **Thrissur** and died in 2024. She asked for a job there on **compassionate grounds**.
She was refused because **Rule 7(37)** of the Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules, 2002 barred women from toddy shops **in any role**.
She went to the High Court and challenged the rule itself.

slides.label: What the State argued
slides.title: The ban was for women's **safety**
bullets: The State said toddy shops are often in **remote** places, so keeping women out protects them from harassment.
It also said nobody has a **fundamental right** to work in the liquor trade.
The shop's licensee backed the ban, saying toddy shops are different from foreign liquor shops.

slides.label: What the Court held
slides.title: Protect women, do not **exclude** them
bullets: Justice **P. Gopinath** found the rule neither justified nor **proportionate**, and struck it down.
It violates **Article 14** (equality), **15** (no sex discrimination), **19** (freedom of occupation) and **21** (life and liberty).
The State's duty is to make workplaces safe, not to stop women working in the field they choose.
slides.note: **Law fact:** The Court relied on the Supreme Court's ruling in **Anuj Garg v. Hotel Association of India** (2008).

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: What this ruling does and **does not** do
bullets: Her claim for a job must now be **considered** without the rule. The Court did not itself give her the job.
Any licence condition based on the rule **cannot stand**. The ruling is about this Kerala rule.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Can the law keep women out of a job "for their own safety"? The Kerala High Court says no 👩‍💼⚖️

A widow whose husband worked at a toddy shop in Thrissur asked for a job there on compassionate grounds after his death. She was turned down because Rule 7(37) of the Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules, 2002 barred women from working in toddy shops in any role. The State defended the rule as a safety measure, saying toddy shops are often in remote places.

Justice P. Gopinath struck the rule down. The Court found it was neither justified nor proportionate, and that it violates Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21 of the Constitution. Relying on the Supreme Court's ruling in Anuj Garg v. Hotel Association of India, the Court said the State's job is to make workplaces safe for women, not to bar them from the work they choose.

What happens now? Her claim for compassionate appointment must be considered without applying the rule, and any licence condition based on it cannot stand. The Court did not itself order that she be given the job.

Case: Sophy v. State of Kerala, WP(C) No. 27762 of 2024, 2026 LiveLaw (Ker) 606 (Kerala High Court)
